headline: FIFA's new rule: Paraguay's Almiron sent off for covering mouth
summary: Miguel Almiron becomes the first player to receive a red card under a new FIFA regulation aimed at combating racism on the field.
details: Paraguay's Miguel Almiron has made an unwanted piece of football history. He became the first player to be sent off for covering his mouth during an on-field confrontation under new FIFA rules.
The incident occurred during the World Cup Group D match between Paraguay and Turkey in Santa Clara, California. Almiron was dismissed in first-half stoppage time after a VAR review.
At the time of the dismissal, Paraguay were leading 1-0. The red card was issued because Almiron appeared to direct a comment at Turkey's Mert Muldur while covering his mouth with his hand.

FIFA announced in April that players who cover their mouths during confrontations with opponents will now be given a red card. This initiative is part of a broader effort to combat racism in the sport.

The rule change follows a controversy involving Benfica winger Gianluca Prestianni, who was accused of racially abusing Vinicius Junior in February. Prestianni was later banned for six matches for homophobic conduct.
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has strongly supported the law, stating that players should not hide their mouths when speaking to opponents if they have nothing to hide.

headline_marked: 32 shots, 0 goals: [[10-man Paraguay eliminate Turkey]] from World Cup
headline: 32 shots, 0 goals: 10-man Paraguay eliminate Turkey from World Cup
summary: Despite dominating possession and firing 32 attempts, Turkey suffered a shock 1-0 defeat to a resilient Paraguay in Group D.
details: Ten-man Paraguay secured a dramatic 1-0 victory over Turkey in a Group D match on Friday, knocking their opponents out of the World Cup. Matias Galarza scored the fastest goal of the tournament so far, rifling in a long-range shot just 64 seconds into the game.

Turkey dominated the match, recording 79% possession at one point and logging 32 attempts on goal. However, poor finishing proved fatal as they failed to score despite numerous chances for stars like Kenan Yildiz and Arda Guler.

The match took a tense turn in the second half when Paraguay's Miguel Almiron was sent off for remarks made to Mert Muldur. Despite playing with 10 men, Paraguay defended resolutely to protect their narrow lead until the final whistle.

The result confirms the United States as Group D winners following their 2-0 win over Australia. For Turkey, the loss marks a miserable early exit from the competition after a similar high-shooting, low-scoring performance in their opening match.

Paraguay, known as 'La Albirroja', has kept their World Cup hopes alive. This is their first appearance in the tournament since 2010, where they reached the quarter-finals before being eliminated by Spain.
